text: ig-post has about 440px of unshaped band between the supporting line (ends ~740) and the mark (~1180), about 33% of the canvas, and the right 47% is empty. Raise the headline from 186px to 233px (two lines "Add a" / "desk.", line height 1.0, top at 81px), and the supporting line from its current size to 61px at line height 1.3, 96px below "desk.". The band then falls to under 400px.

linkedin leaves the right 40% and a 235px band under the supporting line empty. Set the headline at 186px on two lines ("Add a" / "desk.", line height 1.0, top at 72px), move the supporting line into a right column starting at x=640 at 31px, line height 1.3, with its last baseline on the baseline of "desk.", and keep the mark bottom left.

this is the first type-only card anyone would make. Make the type the image: on both sizes "desk." at 186/233px must span at least 45% of the width, and the right-column supporting line on linkedin gives the landscape a split no template does. No new elements.

the "f f" join in "brief file" opens a visible hole on ig-post. Set font-kerning normal and font-feature-settings "kern" 1, "liga" 1 on the body. Keep headline tracking at -0.02em on both sizes and check it matches on linkedin.
snap every vertical gap to the 8px grid: 96px headline to supporting on ig-post, mark baseline 135px above the bottom on ig-post and 40px on linkedin, and left margin 72px on both.

at both sizes the space between "brief" and "file." looks like a double space. Make sure the source has a single space, then set font-kerning normal and font-feature-settings "liga" 1 on the supporting line so the word gap matches "One registry line."

on linkedin the cap top of "Add a" sits about 96px down while the left margin is 72px. Raise the headline block 16px so the cap top lands at about 80px. Then drop the mark so its baseline is 40px above the bottom edge (now about 52px), per the Art Director's note.

on ig-post the empty band from the supporting line (about y790) to the mark (about y1180) is about 390px, 29% of the canvas. That is inside the limit, but it reads as left-over space. Widen the gap under "desk." from about 104px to 152px so the supporting group moves down 48px and the band shrinks to about 340px, under 25%.

the strongest move on the card is the linkedin supporting line sitting on the baseline of "desk." at x≈640. Keep it exactly as built, and on linkedin bump the supporting line from about 28px to 31px so its x-height reads against the headline.

linkedin: headline 95px to 119px, set on 3 lines "A design studio / inside your coding / agent." with its top edge 40px from the top. Supporting line top 40px under the last line, mark bottom edge 40px from the bottom, left edge 72px for all three. The block then fills the card, not just the top half, and no band over 627/3 = 209px is left behind it.
linkedin: the 119px headline is the move. It should run to within 56px of the right edge so it reads as type set to the canvas, not a template headline floating in it. Do not add any other element.

ig-post: supporting line top from about 800px to 704px, which is 244px under the headline's last line. It then reads as the tail of the headline block, not a line floating midway, and the band above the mark becomes about 440px, still under the 450px limit. Keep the mark bottom at 136px and the left edge at 65px.

both sizes: shift the headline about 0.04em left so the stems of "A" and "i" optically align with the F of "Free" and the d of "deskstudio.ai". Keep 600 weight, line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, supporting line 31px on linkedin and 39px on ig-post, mark 25px.

linkedin has a widow, "agent." sits alone on line 3. Keep the headline at 119px, 600, line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, and force the breaks "A design studio / inside your / coding agent." so "coding agent" stays together and the rag steps in on purpose.

the supporting line (about 28px now) and the mark (25px) are too close to read as two levels. Supporting line goes to 39px on linkedin and 49px on ig-post, weight 400. Mark stays 25px in #8a8a93. That gives three clear steps: 119/39/25 on linkedin and 149/49/25 on ig-post.

on ig-post the supporting line floats at about 54% height, between a 250px gap and a 435px gap that nothing shapes. Take the headline to 149px with the breaks "A design / studio / inside your / coding agent." (4 lines, about 596px tall, top at 120px). Set the supporting line's top 48px under the headline's last line, and leave the mark alone at 136px from the bottom. The remaining band is about 375px, between headline-plus-supporting-line and the mark, and it reads as intended.

type only at a polite size is what any template makes. Let the scale be the idea instead. ig-post goes to 149px with the stepped rag above, so the block carries the top 55% of the canvas. On linkedin the headline block spans y 80 to 440, so the type fills the left 90% and nothing else competes.

on linkedin the gap from headline to supporting line (about 60px) almost matches the gap from supporting line to mark (about 70px). Set the supporting line's top 40px under the headline's last line so they read as one group, and keep the mark's bottom edge at 40px from the bottom of the card.

"out now." is set at 600 inside a 400 line, so it is emphasised twice. Set it to 400 on both sizes and let #ffb000 alone carry it. That leaves two weights, 600 for the headline and 400 for everything else.

on linkedin the gap from the headline to the supporting line (~50px) and the gap from the supporting line to the mark (~47px) are nearly equal, so the three read as one stack. Move the headline top up from ~100px to 72px so it matches the 73px left margin. Set the supporting line's top 40px under the headline's last line. The mark then stands alone with about 80px above it and its bottom 40px from the edge.

on ig-post the ~365px band under "Free, MIT, out now." reads as leftover space. Move the supporting line down so its top sits at 1104px, 48px above the mark, and make the two a bottom-left group. The headline then stands alone at the top. The band between the two groups becomes about 390px, still under the 450px limit, and now has a shape.
the top-and-bottom split on ig-post in the composition note is the move that takes it past a stock dark OG card. Keep everything else as it is, with no added elements and no second accent.

On linkedin, open the gap between the headline's last baseline (y≈235) and the supporting line's cap height from about 24px to 40px, moving the supporting line down 16px. On ig-post, move the mark baseline from about y=1207 to exactly y=1215, as in Art Director note 5.

Make every grid cell square. On linkedin, use 54x54 cells with 8px gaps, 6 columns by 8 rows, spanning y=72 to y=560, with the mark baseline also at y=560. On ig-post, use 110x110 cells with 8px gaps, 8 columns by 6 rows, moving the grid top from y=504 to y=456 so it ends at y=1156, above the mark.

The cells now read as 59x53 (linkedin) and 110x100 (ig-post) tiles. The "real pixels" idea depends on the amber cell being a true square pixel, so lock the amber cell to the same square size as its neighbours at both sizes. Keep its position: linkedin column 3, row 4; ig-post column 5, row 3.

on ig-post, set the gap between "November 8." and the supporting line to 80px (currently about 100px), so the headline and the supporting line read as one group. On linkedin, keep the gaps as they are.

on ig-post, take the supporting line from 39px to 49px at line height 1.3, keeping the mark at 16px with its baseline on 1215px. This cuts the empty band from about 370px to under 300px, so the type block carries the canvas instead of leaving the air over.

on both sizes, shift the headline 4px left so the round "O", "S" and "N" align optically with the "B" stem of the supporting line and the "f" of the mark. That machined edge is what makes this Ferro's card and not a template's.

ig-post has an empty band of about 520px (38% of 1350) between the subline and the mark, over the one-third limit. Raise the headline from 149px to 186px, line height 1.0, tracking -0.03em, top at 72px. Force four lines with
: "A bike / crank, from / a spare / bedroom." That ends the block near y=820.

linkedin has the same fault. The block ends at y=280 and leaves about 255px of dead white above the mark. Raise the headline from 86px to 119px, line height 1.0, top at 48px. Force three lines with
: "A bike crank, / from a spare / bedroom." The block should end near y=405.

with the two changes above, the ladder is 186/119 headline, 39/31 supporting and 25 mark, still three roles per size. Supporting line at line height 1.3, 48px under the headline on ig-post and 24px on linkedin. Keep "bedroom." alone on the last line in #e5173f on both sizes.

on ig-post, the gap from the headline baseline to the subline is about 80px. Set it to 48px. The mark's bottom edge sits at 135px from the canvas bottom on ig-post and 40px on linkedin, both 72px from the left, so the mark, subline and headline share one 72px left edge.

at its current size this is the stock type-only card. The 186px four-line stack on ig-post and the 119px three-line stack on linkedin turn it into a poster where "bedroom." lands as the punchline. Do not add any other element.

linkedin headline sets as four lines ("A bike / crank, from / a spare / bedroom."), which breaks the three-line landscape cap, and AD note 4 was not applied. Set it at 119px, line height 1.0, tracking -0.03em, max-width 1056px, with forced breaks "A bike crank, / from a spare / bedroom.". Keep only "bedroom." in #e5173f.

linkedin uses the left 48% and leaves the right half empty, which is a portrait layout on a landscape canvas. With the 119px three-line set above, the headline block runs about 780px wide and 357px tall from top 48px, so the type carries the canvas the way it does on ig-post. Add no element.

linkedin supporting line 31px, 24px under the headline baseline. Mark 25px, bottom left at x 72px, bottom edge 40px from the canvas bottom, so it no longer sits 50px under the subline as one group. On ig-post, confirm the subline is 48px under the headline baseline; it renders at about 44px.
on linkedin, separate the subline (31px) and the mark (25px) by at least 64px vertically so the mark reads third and not as part of the supporting line. The layout above gives about 70px.

hold the type-only route with no added shape or rule. The lift is scale on landscape, as in the typography note. Hang the "A" optically 4px left on both sizes so its diagonal lines up visually with the subline and mark at x 72px.
verbatim and locked by the brief, no change.

on ig-post the vertical scale floats 8px off the left edge with no spine, so it reads detached from the 8px top bar. Add an 8px #0a0a0a spine at x 0–8 from y 810 to 1350 and hang the ticks from it, matching the linkedin spine at x 660.

the ig-post grey field (about 960x420 below the corner) is mostly empty. On ig-post, lengthen the long ticks from 104px to 160px and the mid ticks from 64px to 104px on both scales, and grow the empty corner square to 160x160. On linkedin, lengthen the long ticks from 104px to 120px. Both changes let the ruler carry the panel instead of edging it.

the ruler reads as a desk ruler, not as 0.01mm. Halve the minor tick pitch from 8px to 4px at 1px #737373 on both scales, so the fine graduation reads as a dense band no school ruler has. Keep the long and mid pitch at 80px and 40px.

linkedin only: "made." is a one-word widow on line 3. Cap the black claim's max-width at about 780px so it breaks "Fits every Ferro / ever made." Keep it at 3 lines total. Leave ig-post's 4-line break as it is.

linkedin only: the supporting line floats about 145px under "made.", so it doesn't read with the headline. Set its top 40px under the headline's last baseline (about y=385). Keep `ferro.tools` at bottom left, baseline no lower than y=589.

linkedin only: the headline leaves about 220px empty on the right. Take it from 95 to 119px (on scale), line height 1.0, -0.02em. The red figure then spans about 685px and the 3-line block carries the canvas. Sizes become 119 / 31 / 20.
hold the move. The red spec as the headline is the brand's own voice. Don't add a rule, bar or shape to fill the ig-post bottom band.

on ig-post the #ebe8e0 block runs from y 540 to the bottom and holds one line at its top, which leaves about 515px (38% of the canvas) empty. Move the block top from y 540 to y 810 so the canvas splits 60/40. Put "Battery now included." 64px under the new block top at 49px. Keep the mark 136px from the bottom. The largest gap is then about 350px (26%).

ig-post headline from 95px to 119px with the same three spans, line height 1.05, tracking -0.02em, top 88px, left 64px. It then ends near y 465, inside the top 40%, and "to break even." runs about 780px wide, inside the 952px column.

on linkedin, the gap under the supporting line (about 140px) is wider than the gaps inside the headline group, so the right 40% looks unused rather than planned. Fix this with the originality note below, and keep every gap a multiple of 8.

carry the split to linkedin so both sizes make the same move. Add a full-height #ebe8e0 block from x 768 to the right edge. Move "Battery now included." (31px, 400) into it at left 816px, with its baseline on the mark's baseline 40px from the bottom. The headline and the mark stay on the paper on the left.

linkedin: remove the empty right panel (x 768 to 1200). Add a full-width #ebe8e0 band from y 487 to the bottom edge. Set "Battery now included." inside it at 31px weight 400, left 72, vertically centred in the band. Move the mark into the same band at bottom right, 72px from the right and on the same baseline. Both sizes then share one system: the headline on paper, the news on the surface band.
linkedin and ig-post: set the mark colour #161614 to #6b6a66, so "Battery now included." clearly reads second and the mark reads third.

linkedin: move the headline block down about 8px so the cap top of "Seven years" sits 72px from the top edge, matching the 72px left margin. ig-post: move the band top from y 810 to y 760 and keep the supporting line 64px below it, so the gap from headline to band (about 300px) is close to the gap from the line to the mark.
once the band carries both sizes, change nothing else. The move is the hard tint split under a number-led headline, and it must look the same on both sizes. Add no rule, icon or second element.
on linkedin, raise "Battery now included." from 31px to 39px, weight 400, so it stops sitting one step above the 25px mark and reads as the clear second voice.

on ig-post, the 305px of paper between the headline and the band equals the 305px between the supporting line and the mark. Move the band top from y 760 to y 680, keep the supporting line 64px under the band top, and keep the mark 136px from the bottom.

on linkedin, take the headline from 95px to 119px with line height 1.05 and tracking -0.02em, top 48px, left 72px. The block then ends near y 423 and carries the empty right half, with 64px of paper above the band at y 487.

once the ig-post band starts at y 680, the paper and surface split the canvas exactly in half. Keep "Seven years / to break even. / Then free." wholly on the paper above it. The split then reads as a deliberate before and after rather than a footer strip.

linkedin only. The headline moves from 95px to 119px, line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, still on 2 lines ("Now installing in" / "Minneapolis."). Line 1 then spans about 906px of the 1056px measure. The cap top stays at y=40. Keep the supporting line at 31px with its baseline at y=520, and the mark at 25px with its baseline at y=572. The empty band between the headline and the supporting line drops from about 250px (40% of the height) to about 190px (under a third), and the right-hand 34% of the canvas stops reading as leftover.

linkedin is currently the default OG title card: a small headline top left and a footer bottom left. The 119px move above is the fix. "Minneapolis." becomes about 708px wide in orange and reads as the image, not a title. On ig-post, keep the "Now / installing in / Minneapolis." stair rag exactly as it is, because it is the one move here a template would not make.
both sizes. Pull the headline left by -0.04em (about -6px at 149px, -5px at 119px) so the N and M stems sit optically on x=72. Today they sit about 6px inside the supporting line and the mark.

linkedin, after the headline change, set the gap from the headline's last baseline to the supporting line's cap top to 192px, so it lands on the 8px grid. ig-post spacing holds: about 215px above the supporting block, about 270px below it, and the mark baseline at y≈1200 inside the 10% bottom zone.

linkedin only: raise the supporting line from 31px to 39px, weight 400, line height 1.3. At 31 it sits one step above the 25px mark and the two read as one tier. linkedin scale becomes 95 / 39 / 25. Leave ig-post at 149 / 61 / 25.

linkedin only: move the supporting line's top from y≈430 to y=376 (about 80px under the headline's descender). Keep the mark baseline at y≈572. The supporting line then groups with the headline and the mark stands alone in the corner, instead of the line floating between them.
ig-post: keep the supporting block top at y=760 and the mark baseline at y=1215. Do not let either gap (≈230 above, ≈285 below) go past 450px when the linkedin fixes land, because the DOM is shared.
no layout change this round. The confident move is the 149px stack on ig-post with "Minneapolis." on its own line. No fix may shrink it or rewrap it.

ig-post, tighten the figure group. Close the gap from the "takes" line to the $400 cap top, now about 52px, to 32px. Close the gap from the $400 baseline to "off their quote.", now about 50px, to 32px. Both gaps then sit at the same ratio as on linkedin. Add -0.02em tracking on $400.
linkedin, move the right-panel text from x=708 to x=736. That gives a 72px inset from the panel edge at 664, close to the 72px left margin, so both columns share one margin.

ig-post, move the top of the #ebe8e0 block from y=432 to y=536 and start the label at y=616. Keep the headline at y=110. The headline zone then takes the top 40%, the gap between the figure group and the mark drops from about 330px to under 300px, and the block is no longer two thirds of the canvas.

ig-post, set "off their quote." on the $400 baseline, to the right of the figure, starting at x=688 and still 25px/400. The sentence then runs through the number in one line, and it fills the empty right 40% beside $400.

ig-post, the gap from the supporting line to the grid measures about 48px on screen. Set it to 64px as the AD asked, and take the 16px from the grid height (496 to 480) so the mark still sits above y 1215. linkedin, put the mark's baseline on the grid's bottom edge at y 579.

the tiles show at about 1.1:1 against their frame and read as empty image boxes at low brightness. Change the frame and gutter colour from surface #ebe8e0 to muted #6b6a66 at 30% over #f7f5f0. Tiles stay #f7f5f0. This is a tint of the palette, not a new hue.

ig-post, remove the 16px outer frame band so the 4x3 tiles sit straight on the paper with 8px gutters. That fixes the box inside a box, and the grid's left and right edges line up with the text column at x 72 and x 1008.

the twelve tiles read as a blank panel grid. Make the tile proportions panel-like on both sizes (portrait tiles about 1:1.5 on linkedin as now, and portrait tiles on ig-post as well, 6 columns x 2 rows instead of landscape 4x3) so the panel reading is unmistakable.

linkedin, the right 45% of the card is unused space and the left stack is the stock type-only layout. Take the rule out of the linkedin layout. Move "Pay when the fourth one matters." into the right column at 40px/400 #ededf0, line height 1.35, broken after "fourth" (two lines). Set its left edge at x=704 and put the last line's baseline on the "Always." baseline, so the payoff answers the headline across the card. The mark stays bottom left at 23px muted, baseline 38px from the bottom.

ig-post, the 390px under "quill.app" is leftover space. Move the mark down to the bottom-left safe line, baseline at y=1215. Keep the rule at y=808 and the supporting line 40px below it. The mark then holds the corner and no band is taller than about 300px.
ig-post, end the rule at x=832 (the right edge of "drafts.") instead of x=1008, so it matches the headline's width. Keep it 1px #8b8d99.

ig-post, the gap from "Always." to the rule (about 290px) and the gap from the supporting line to "quill.app" (about 290px) are the same size, so two unrelated gaps look identical. Move the rule down from y=808 to y=864 and keep the supporting line 40px below it. That leaves about 344px under the headline and about 248px above the mark, so the bottom group reads as one unit and the headline band stays under a third of the canvas. Leave the mark's baseline at y=1215.

linkedin, the rule from note 4 is missing. Add a 1px rule in #8b8d99 from x=704 to x=1128, 40px above the cap height of "Pay", so it lines up with the supporting line's column. The left-margin rule to x=640 would cross the headline.

ig-post, the supporting group floats in the middle of the canvas. With the move above it should sit in the bottom 40%, as the portrait pattern asks. Check that the rule's right end still lines up with the period of "drafts." at x=832.

keep the type-only restraint and make one move a template would not. On ig-post, run the rule from x=72 to the right edge at x=1080, full bleed on that side only, so it reads like a page edge. Keep it 1px in #8b8d99.

on ig-post, take the headline from 169px to 226px (still "Cut it." / "It" / "stays.", line height 1.0, -0.02em) and set the headline block's top at 96px. Right now there is a band of about 458px between the supporting line (bottom about 722px) and the mark (top about 1184px), which is over a third of 1350. At 226px the headline ends near 774px and the supporting line near 870px, so the band drops to about 314px, and "Cut it." fills about 615px of the 936px column instead of 460px.

this is the type-only card any template would make. Give "Cut it." a line-through in muted #8b8d99, 0.06em thick, sitting at 0.32em above the baseline, and keep the glyphs in #ededf0 so the words stay legible. The cut sentence then stays visible, which is the product. Keep the accent only on "stays.", on both sizes.

on linkedin, the supporting line and the mark are both 30px and differ only by colour. Set the supporting line to 40px, weight 400, line height 1.3, to match ig-post, and keep the mark at 30px. On ig-post, set the lone "It" line flush to the same optical left edge as "Cut" and "stays.": nudge it -0.04em so the I's serif lines up with the C.

on linkedin, start the headline's top at 64px and keep 48px down to the supporting line, then put the mark's baseline 40px from the bottom. The gap between the supporting line and the mark must stay at least 56px, so the mark does not read as part of the supporting group. Check that every vertical gap is a multiple of 8.

ig-post: there is about 80px of visible air between "It" and "stays." but only about 64px between "Cut it." and "It", so the gaps don't match. Pull the "stays." line up 16px (margin-top -16px) so the three lines read as one evenly set block.

linkedin: the headline block only fills the left 43% of the canvas, so the right half is empty space with no shape. Take the headline from 127px to 169px (brand scale; ig-post already uses this size, so the card still has three sizes). That makes "It stays." about 590px wide and lets the block carry the left half. Keep the 72px left margin, the supporting line 48px below the headline, and the mark where it is.

linkedin, the break "with the / room." leaves "the" hanging at a line end. Keep three lines but break as "The page dims / with the room. /" only if it fits in 1056px at 127px. If not, keep the current breaks and pull the headline's left edge back about 4px so the overhang of "T" and "w" lines up optically with the 72px column that the supporting line and mark sit on.

linkedin, AD note 3 is not done. The supporting line still sits about 72px under "room." and the mark about 40px under the supporting line, so the three read as one stack. Move the supporting line up so its cap top is 48px under the "room." baseline. Drop the mark to baseline 587px (40px from the bottom). The gap between the supporting line and the mark should end up close to twice the gap between the headline and the supporting line.

linkedin, the right 45% beside "with the / room." is left over, not shaped. Push the headline from 127px to 135px, which is inside the scale tolerance, so line 1 ends near x 990. On ig-post, raise the supporting line and the mark group by 0px but check that the band between 900 and 1180px stays under 300px. It is under that now, so keep it.

the step-by-step dim is the idea, so make the steps exact. Set line 2 ("with the") to one flat tint midway between `#ededf0` and `#8b8d99` (about `#bcbdc5`), and set "room." to flat `#8b8d99`, instead of a continuous gradient across the lines. Three clean steps read as a dimmer switch. A smear reads as an effect.

linkedin, delete the 1px rule at y 241 (x 72–552). Set the cut-out to x 72–712, y 200–552 as one clean rectangle, with stubs at x 0–72 and bars resuming at x 712 on every row inside it. ig-post, the lower 64% (y 480–1350) is one unbroken stripe field. Move "Now on your phone." out of the top cut-out into a bottom-left cut-out (x 72–520, y 1144–1232), set at x 120 on the same baseline as quill.app (y 1200), so the two groups bracket the field. Shrink the top cut-out to y 80–392, which leaves 48px clear below "train.".

linkedin headline from 72 to 95px (brand scale), line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, still two lines. With "train." ending near x 664, the cut-out edge at x 712 now sits a deliberate 48px past it. ig-post subhead from 30 to 40px so it holds its own against the 127px headline. Keep the mark at 23px on both sizes.

linkedin, end the rows at y 80, 120 and 160 at x 984 so quill.app sits on bare background with at least 48px clear on all sides, matching ig-post. The row at y 160 currently runs to 1200 directly under the mark.

make the field read as prose, not stripes. Drop one row (an 80px gap) after every 5–6 rows as a paragraph break, and end each paragraph's last row at 30–45% of the width. Keep the bars #171923 and 16px tall on the 40px rhythm.
ig-post, the bars on rows y 1160 and 1200 start at x 520, only 16px after "phone." ends (about x 504). Start them at x 552 so there is 48px of clear space, and keep the end at x 864.

ig-post, AD note 2 is only half applied. Add the 72px right stubs (x 1008–1080) on rows y 120, 200, 240 and 320, and add the missing left stub (x 0–72) on row y 240. Every row from y 80 to 360 should then carry both stubs, so the cut-out reads as one rectangle (x 72–1008, y 80–375).

linkedin, the right edge of the cut-out breaks at y 200–240. Add bars from x 712 on row y 200 (end x 936) and row y 240 (end x 1104), so the edge is one straight line at x 712 from y 200 to 455. Leave rows y 80–160 ending at x 984 so the mark keeps its bare patch.

ig-post, the bar field from y 400 to 1100 (about 52% of the canvas) reads as an empty dark band at thumbnail size and low brightness. On both sizes, make the bars 24px tall on the same 40px pitch (16px gaps), still #171923, so the "page" shows in the feed.

the same bar-length set (994 / 691 / 432 / 842) repeats in every paragraph block on ig-post, which reads as a pattern rather than a page. Within a block, use no length twice: vary in 8px steps between 320 and 1080, and end each block with its shortest line.
linkedin, add the missing 72px left stub at x 0–72 on row y 240, so the stubs run every 40px from y 200 to y 480 and the cut-out reads as one rectangle, as it does on ig-post.
linkedin, the right bar column stops at y 440 and leaves a pocket at x 712–1200, y 480–540. Add one bar at y 480 from x 712 to 1008 so the column ends level with the last left stub.

linkedin, the right 55% of the canvas (x 530 to 1162) is left over. Move the supporting line into a right column at x 640. Set it as two lines, "One brief file." / "One registry line.", at 39px, line height 1.3. Align the baseline of its last line to the baseline of "desk." (about y 385). Keep the mark bottom left with its baseline 38px above the bottom edge. The band from "desk." to the mark is then about 175px, under 209px.

ig-post, the band from the supporting line (bottom about 730px) to the mark (top about 1175px) is about 445px. That is 5px under the 450px limit, and nothing shapes it. Raise the supporting line from 61px to 76px, line height 1.3, and keep the 64px gap under "desk.". The block should end near 790px and the band drop to about 385px. Keep the headline at its current size and position in the top 40%. Keep the mark on the 10% bottom margin.

the stacked type-only layout is the first one anyone would make. The linkedin split above, with the supporting line hung off the "desk." baseline in its own column, is the one move that makes it ours. Do not add any other element.
